Internal Assessment for the month of October 2020"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\"This is my submission for the Bimonthly internal assessment for the month of October.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMost of the information here have been collected from different reference sites, the links to which have been mentioned. The points copy pasted have been put in quotes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe questions to the cases being discussed can be viewed from the link below 👇\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/medicinedepartment.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/medicine-paper-for-october-2020-first.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe first case presented to us is\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"arial, tahoma, helvetica, freesans, sans-serif\" style=\"color: #222222;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 15.84px;\"\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?hl=en\u0026amp;q=https:\/\/swathibogari158.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/chronic-decompensated-liver-disease.html\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1601299903798000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNH85nubjcIL4Y0ah49NOlBa0oj3aw\" href=\"https:\/\/swathibogari158.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/chronic-decompensated-liver-disease.html\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/swathibogari158.\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Eblogspot.com\/2020\/09\/chronic-\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Edecompensated-liver-disease.\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Ehtml\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E57 year old man who has been an alcoholic since the past 40 years complaining of yellowish discoloration of sclera, abdominal distension \u0026amp; bilateral pedal edema since 3 years with a history of bilious vomitings and bleeding from gums. He also had a history of multiple blebs on his right lower limb for which debridement was done 2 years back. Patient has also been apparently taking loads of self medications over the last 4 months.Since 1 month he has been abdominal distension, Dyspnea on exertion. He also has been having reduced memory, depression \u0026amp; fear of dying. Over the last 5 days he has been having Multiple blebs on his left lower limb. He has also been having intermittent dark stools since the past 1 week.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAnatomical location : Liver - Acute Decompensated Liver failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEtiological factors : Alcohol, over consumption of over the counter drugs such as NSAIDS and antibiotics.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1.Ascites\u003C\/b\u003E is due to accumulation of fluid and salt retention along with portal hypertension.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPortal hypertension occurs due to increased hepatic resistance. Hepatic resistance occurs due to increased hepatic fibrosis as in cirrhosis and due to activation of stellate cells causing fibrogenesis. There is reduced production of endothelial nitric oxide synthase which leads to increased vasoconstriction.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is also increased systemic circulatory nitric oxide as well as increased vascular endothelial growth factor \u0026amp; tumor necrosis factor that result in in splanchnic arterial vasodilation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESplanchnic vasodilation leads to pooling of blood leads to decrease in circulating volume. This leads to compensatory vasoconstriction through the release of Antidiurectic hormone. This leads to free water retention and activation of Sympathetic nervous system and Renin angiotension aldosterone system which furthermore increases retention of renal sodium and water retention.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe information above was learnt from Harrison's Principals of internal medicine.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgJQGC0baV0z_uDqxz5jo8AdsRRSwCgfRFB5nofVYZUJ_XUnntD80fhItytoT1ttJuc5ZB1nvmLw4kGTou5NqLVFSPCl0ETPUVIywgrx4dXTTH9bi39AHeoNpngG5KpRikpdyH6iRATnhg\/s545\/Screenshot+%252829%2529.png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"545\" data-original-width=\"388\" height=\"640\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgJQGC0baV0z_uDqxz5jo8AdsRRSwCgfRFB5nofVYZUJ_XUnntD80fhItytoT1ttJuc5ZB1nvmLw4kGTou5NqLVFSPCl0ETPUVIywgrx4dXTTH9bi39AHeoNpngG5KpRikpdyH6iRATnhg\/w456-h640\/Screenshot+%252829%2529.png\" width=\"456\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/notes.medicosnotes.com\/2015\/04\/pathophysiology-of-ascites-in-cirrhosis.html\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/notes.medicosnotes.com\/2015\/04\/pathophysiology-of-ascites-in-cirrhosis.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere are two theories stated so far on the formation of\u0026nbsp; Ascites :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.mayoclinicproceedings.org\/article\/S0025-6196(11)63752-X\/fulltext\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.mayoclinicproceedings.org\/article\/S0025-6196(11)63752-X\/fulltext\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) The underfill theory\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) The overfill theory\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe underfill theory states that Hypovolemia\u0026nbsp; leads to stimulation of Juxtagolerular cells to release renin which releases angiotensin 1 which is converted to angiotensin 2 by ACE leading to aldosterone release from zona glomerulosa and increased retention of salt and water leading to ascites\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe overfill theory states that hypervolemia along with portal hypertension results in overflow from portal system to the peritoneal cavity leading to ascites\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2\u003C\/b\u003E.\u003Cb\u003EBipedal edema \u003C\/b\u003Eis due to fluid and salt retention and also due to hypoalbuminaemia. Albumin plays an important role in maintaining capillary oncotic pressure.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EReduced albumin leads to reduced capillary oncotic pressure leading to fluid leakage into the interstitial space.Further more long standing pedal edema lead to long standing venous stasis, lymphatic drainage obstruction and on top of that over the counter use of NSAIDS and corticosterioids lead to recurrent bleb formation along with ulcerations and cellulitis. Also Patients with liver failure are immunocompromised and are more prone to infections.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttp:\/\/rnceus.com\/lf\/lfalb.html\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) \u003Cb\u003EAsterixis and constructional apraxia\u003C\/b\u003E are features of Hepatic encephalopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHepatic encephalopathy is a syndrome in patients with liver failure. It is characterized by neuropsychiatric abnormalities due to accumulation of neurotoxic substances in the brain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E'Ammonia is usually produced by bacteria in the gastrointestinal tract from the breakdown product of amino acids and urea followed by metabolism and clearance by the liver. In liver failure there is either a decrease in the number of functioning hepatocytes, portosystemic shunting, or both, resulting in decreased ammonia clearance and hyperammonemia.'\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOnce ammonia crosses the blood brain barrier, it has multiple neurotoxic effects.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThese include alterations in molecular transport (e.g. amino acids, electrolytes, water) in astrocytes and neurons, increased synthesis of glutamine from glutamate by astrocytes, inhibition of excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potential generation, impaired amino acid metabolism, and impaired energy utilization as a result of increased GABA activity.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAsterixis is inability to maintain postural stability. Abnormal diencephalic function leads to flapping tremors when patient helds arms and wrists in extension.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERisk factors for Asterixis include Infection, GI bleed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUsually the underlying cause needs to be\u0026nbsp; addressed. Removal of ammonia by using laxatives such as lactulose and also addressing other risk factors such as infection by putting the patient on an antibiotic is required which was well addressed by the treating team.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESome of these useful points were found from the link below\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.unboundmedicine.com\/5minute\/view\/5-Minute-Clinical-Consult\/117471\/all\/Hepatic_Encephalopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4\u003C\/b\u003E.\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;Treatment efficacies\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Col style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003E\u0026nbsp;Fluid and salt restriction along with Diuretic such as Furosemide have been advised which is addressing the fluid overload status of the patient.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EThe patient has also been put on Antibiotics such as Augmentin and Metrogyl for his cellulitis. The swab culture report from the ulcer shows sensitivity to Augmentin.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ERifaximin and Lactulose is a frequently used combination in patients with Hepatic encephalopathy.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ol\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;Here's a randomized, double blinded controlled trial comparing Rifaximin plus lactulose versus the use of lactulose alone in patients with hepatic encephalopathy.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"goog_529309234\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23877348\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/23877348\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP- 120 patients with overt Hepatic encephalopathy were randomized into two groups\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI-Group A lactulose plus rifaximin 1,200 mg\/day, 63 participants\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGroup B\u0026nbsp; received lactulose\u0026nbsp; plus placebo. This group had 57 participants.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC- Combination of rifaximin plus lactulose was found to be more effective than lactulose alone\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EO - 48 patients in group A compared to 29 patients in group B had complete reversal of hepatic encephalopathy. Reduced mortality in group A vs Group B - 23.8% vs. 49.1%. There were more deaths in group B because of sepsis compared to group A - 7 deaths in group A and 17 in group B. And patients on lactulose plus rifaximin had shorter hospital stay. There were no differences noted in GI bleed or hepatorenal syndrome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) Syrup Hepamerz consists of L-ornithine, L- aspartate. This reduces the accumulation of ammonia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThis is a randomized prospective controlled trial carried out from May 2004 to February 2006 at Mexico city comparing L- ornithine L Aspartate to lactulose\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.sciencedirect.com\/science\/article\/pii\/S1665268119319891\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP- 20 participants with cirrhosis were included in this study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI- 10 received LOLA\u0026nbsp; at a dosage of 9grams for 2 weeks ( 1 sachet containing 3 grams for 3 times a day) where as the other 10 participants received lactulose at a dosage of 30 ml per day for 2 weeks ( syrup containing 67 grams lactulose\/100ml)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC- LOLA was found to be more effective in reducing hyperammonemic hepatic encephalopathy in Mexican patients with cirrhosis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EO -\u0026nbsp; They were compared on the basis of mental state, number connection test, blood ammonia levels,asterixis, portal systemic encephalopathy index, EEGs, Quality of life assessment \u0026amp; GI side effects.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjmyDAT65nytBGLPcydPWbdwjUBMq5VlYLVrUC3P8Kykj6JJkZ5jO2yxN0s4u80yl3DXXUIPD91RZT5sAnGqacqFJCN_2NICcGhjzLYmvp8oo8act7MyVggpxz4o3TqIONBs5l0gVJBRFc\/s1080\/lola.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"931\" data-original-width=\"1080\" height=\"552\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjJW1yHA_KjeaH-BRMEP4yEaX_owRzsHUve1etEyWkX7V2mpFcJtGWSSsnu3y6-n_6ybUL-6U6VsaLBLDw5_F7txx1wCI_I_oJYHcaIpUyqIp1IIJY_hZg0azkhPGhsvLxTiU4qJWQfna0\/w640-h552\/LOLA2.jpeg\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u0026nbsp;Even though both the study groups showed improvement,, the participants receiving LOLA showed more improvement comparitively.\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAnother Randomised control placebo controlled study on LOLA\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/18983791\/\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EP - \u003C\/b\u003E80 cirrhotic patients were enrolled in this study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI- 80 patients were divided into two groups.\u0026nbsp; One receiving 20g\/day L-ornithine L aspartate and other receiving placebo. Both dissolved in 250ml of 55 dextrose and infused intravenously for 4 hours a day for 5 days along with 0.5g\/kg of dietary protein intake everyday\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EC- LOLA infusions were found to be more effective in cirrhotic patients.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EO- Greater improved in mental status, blood ammonia levels were noticed in participants receving LOLA.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5) Udiliv contains ursodeoxycholic acid which has shown to reduce biochemical markers of cholestasis and hepatocellular damge in patients with chronic liver disease.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC1379051\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProtein powder is needed since the patient has significant hypoalbuminaemia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7) And also the Patient should've been started on a non selective beta blocker such a Carvedilol would have been effective in preventing recurrent epsiodes of GI bleed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/aasldpubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1002\/hep.23689\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003ESecond case:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?hl=en\u0026amp;q=https:\/\/sainiharika469.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/hello-everyone.html?m%3D1\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1601299903798000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNGWeguCn5K7NX3esaM-hnGhxTdB4A\" href=\"https:\/\/sainiharika469.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/hello-everyone.html?m=1\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/sainiharika469.\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Eblogspot.com\/2020\/09\/hello-\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Eeveryone.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E54 year old man who has been consuming large amounts of alcohol since 1 year was diagnosed an year back with\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3 Seizures episodes\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EChronic pancreatitis\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECholeliathiasis\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAlcoholic liver disease\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECovid positive\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDiabetic since 8 years\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHypertensive since 3 years\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDiagnosed to be pulmonary kochs positive 1 month back\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHe presented to us with the complains of abdominal tightness, bilateral pedal edema, loose stools\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003Esince 20 days\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn admission he had anemia with leukocytosis, lft was deranged with hypoalbuminaemia (1.6 gm\/dl) and deranged coagulation profile.His CT abdomen showed reduced diameters of intra hepatic portion of IVC and hepatic vein and enlarged liver. SAAG is above 1.1 mg\/dl (1.2mg\/dl) - could be due to portal vein thrombosis, Budd Chiari syndrome, Alcoholic hepatitis, Cirrhosis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe was on ATT - on a combination therapy of rifampicin, INH, pyrazinamide and Ethambutol. Among which isoniazid, rifampicin and pyrazinamide are known to cause hepatotoxicity and would've further worsened the patients condition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhLfyvik352JbL7ULt81X5s5U0z3PZ-MxO221n7dREc3p5OoOIl4myzFHkvEyk-kIONwCigcMKH7FV9_b-7J7-aOm3PWExC9YDJ428iXmVyZ2ePKu5w93eA9u0XDA0DclNMhx3EAOxWdmQ\/s930\/isoni.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"930\" data-original-width=\"884\" height=\"640\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhLfyvik352JbL7ULt81X5s5U0z3PZ-MxO221n7dREc3p5OoOIl4myzFHkvEyk-kIONwCigcMKH7FV9_b-7J7-aOm3PWExC9YDJ428iXmVyZ2ePKu5w93eA9u0XDA0DclNMhx3EAOxWdmQ\/w608-h640\/isoni.jpeg\" width=\"608\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u0026nbsp;More on Isoniazide metabolism and other ATT drugs metabolism given in the link below\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.semanticscholar.org\/paper\/Isoniazid-Toxicity-Bhise\/10bee11efbe5adf5aa32c27cb2964352184e81cd\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Given the patients history of prolonged nocturnal fever with sweats, dry cough, generalized weakness and weight loss along with sputum positive for Tuberculosis confirm pulmonary tb in him. His chect Xray PA view also shows\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. The ascites is because of Chronic liver failure. Because of narrowing of vessels in the portal system causing portal hypertension along with\u0026nbsp; hypoalbuminaemia and fluid and salt retention as earlier explained due to activation of sympathetic nervous system.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;All of these three drugs are metabolized by the liver. With the patient having Chronic liver disease there would be further more accumulation of these three drugs in the blood leading to furthermore side effects of these drugs and also more detoriation of the liver status.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGuidelines for reintiating ATT were given by American thoracic society and British Thoracic society.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.thoracic.org\/statements\/resources\/tb-opi\/hepatotoxicity-of-antituberculosis-therapy.pdf\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.thoracic.org\/statements\/resources\/tb-opi\/hepatotoxicity-of-antituberculosis-therapy.pdf\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;'\u003Cb\u003EACCORDING TO ATS -\u0026nbsp;Treatment\nshould be interrupted and, generally, a modified or alternative\nregimen used for those with ALT elevation more than three times\nthe upper limit of normal (ULN) in the presence of hepatitis symptoms and\/or jaundice, or five times the ULN in the absence of\nsymptoms.'\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.researchgate.net\/publication\/41434496_Safety_of_3_Different_Reintroduction_Regimens_of_Antituberculosis_Drugs_after_Development_of_Antituberculosis_Treatment-Induced_Hepatotoxicity\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere's an interesting case of a 22 year old man with pulmonary Kochs and Inferior vena cava thrombosis.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttp:\/\/www.anncaserep.com\/full-text\/accr-v3-id1534.php\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E'Tuberculosis has several mechanisms that induce a hypercoagulable state and can lead thromboembolic complications. Hypercoagulability in tuberculosis is attributed to decreased antithrombin 3 and protein C, elevated plasma fibrinogen level, increased platelet aggregation and reactive thrombocytosis. Antiphospholipid antibody levels are high in\u0026nbsp; patient with tuberculosis, deficiency of protein S have also been mentioned.\u0026nbsp; '\u003Cspan class=\"text-primary\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECertain studies showed that\u0026nbsp;local thrombosis is associated with increased levels of type 1 plasminogen activator inhibitor and tissue factor. Link to the point above have been taken from the links below.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/17473582\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/8617488\/\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) The efficacy of lactulose in chronic liver failure by preventing accumulation of ammonia has already been discussed in the first case.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) Protein powder is needed since the patient has significant hypoalbuminaemia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5) I don't see the need for Piperacillin injections and nebulisation here. Instead the patient should've been started on second line ATT. And TIPS or liver transplant is further going to help the patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3rd case\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?hl=en\u0026amp;q=https:\/\/sushma29.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/ascites-secondary-to-nephrotic-syndrome.html?m%3D1\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1601299903798000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNEaJAwFIjy57te7RQwWRAqWFSi2wA\" href=\"https:\/\/sushma29.blogspot.com\/2020\/09\/ascites-secondary-to-nephrotic-syndrome.html?m=1\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/sushma29.blogspot.com\/\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003E2020\/09\/ascites-secondary-to-\u003Cwbr\u003E\u003C\/wbr\u003Enephrotic-syndrome.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E46 year old man with the complains of bilateral pedal edema since 1 year and abdominal distention since 1 month with a significant proteinuria\u0026nbsp; \u0026gt;2.5 g\/day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEi2jzVofC3YAGLASLSShRTvBRg9WGr66dnYdR_KbXGBZEGAR0avRcpQOt_OIkDY7b-78KlaGajZr7FPefE_FtYBbZPEGt7gc__tsYnJnGnAE99WdWAMS4h7zpCSCyCiq5GM2sFw0SPL8sk\/s575\/Screenshot+%252832%2529.png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"558\" data-original-width=\"575\" height=\"622\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEi2jzVofC3YAGLASLSShRTvBRg9WGr66dnYdR_KbXGBZEGAR0avRcpQOt_OIkDY7b-78KlaGajZr7FPefE_FtYBbZPEGt7gc__tsYnJnGnAE99WdWAMS4h7zpCSCyCiq5GM2sFw0SPL8sk\/w640-h622\/Screenshot+%252832%2529.png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.uspharmacist.com\/article\/nephrotic-syndrome-medication-and-other-related-risks-42540\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.uspharmacist.com\/article\/nephrotic-syndrome-medication-and-other-related-risks-42540\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENephrotic syndrome:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1) fluid restriction \u0026lt;1l\/day along with salt restriction \u0026lt;2g\/day\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) And the patients are started on diuretics.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Anticoagulants if needed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFurthermore the patient on corticosteriods and Immunosuppresants though their efficacy has not been significantly proven yet.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe last to go option would be renal transplant could be through a live organ donar or through Jeevandhan program.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERenal biopsy helps in diagnosing the cause of the nephrotic syndrome\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) The pros of renal biopsy would be\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.Getting to know the cause of nephrotic synrome\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. It would help us decide the treatment plan\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. Prognosis could be assessed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) Cons of renal biopsy :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Bleeding\u0026nbsp; is a common cause that occurs after renal biopsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Infections\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERenal biopsy wouldn't really put him on the road to recovery. Eventually no matter what the cause is the patient would be put either on steriods alone or on a combination of steroids \u0026amp; Immunosuppressants.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere's a randomized controlled trial on cyclophosphamide and steroids in patients with idiopathic membranous nephropathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/jasn.asnjournals.org\/content\/18\/6\/1899\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/jasn.asnjournals.org\/content\/18\/6\/1899\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP-\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EA total of 104 patients were recruited from March 1993 to February 1995: 53 patients in group 1 and 51 in group 2.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EI - Patients were divided into two groups.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EGroup 1 received supportive therapy that consisted of dietary sodium restriction, diuretics, and antihypertensive agents.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EGroup 2 received a 6months course of alternate months of steroid and cyclophosphamide.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EThe treatment regimen consisted of intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g\/d for 3 consecutive days followed by oral prednisolone 0.5 mg\/kg per d for 27 days in the 1st, 3rd, and 5th months and oral cyclophosphamide at 2 mg\/kg per d in the 2nd, 4th, and 6th months.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E'Follow-up visits were scheduled every 2 weeks for 2 months, every month for 6 months, and thereafter every 6 months or more frequently when required. Parameters monitored included 24-h urinary protein and serum creatinine at each visit and serum albumin, cholesterol, and hemoglobin every 6 months.'\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EC -\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #2e2b2b; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px;\"\u003ETreatment with a 6-mo regimen of cyclophosphamide and steroids induces remissions in a high proportion and arrests progression of renal insufficiency\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #2e2b2b; font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 14px;\"\u003EO -\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #2e2b2b; What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 55 year old woman, farmer by occupation with a history of on and off episodes of Shortness of breath since the past 20 years, a known diabetic since the past 8 years and a known hypertensive since the past 20 days presented with the complaints of\u0026nbsp; Shortness of breath since 15 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBilateral pedal edema since 15 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFacial puffiness since 15 says\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EProblem List:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECOPD\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERight heart failure\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA known diabetic since 8 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA known hypertensive since 20 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnatomical localization for her problem:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe localization of her problem is in the heart and the Lungs. She has right heart failure which has exacerbated her COPD. Her HRCT chest reveals brochiectatic changes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPrimary Etiology to the patients problem:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPrimary Etiology\u0026nbsp; of the recent exacerbation\u0026nbsp; is because of right heart failure on the pre existing COPD.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2) What are mechanism of action, indication and efficacy over placebo of each of the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used for this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing Azithromycin or placebo in patients with COPD (AECOPD)\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EP - 301 patients with COPD, had a smoking history of ≥10 pack-years and one or more exacerbations in the previous year were randomized (1:1) within 48 hours of hospital admission\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI - Azithromycin (\u003Ci\u003En\u003C\/i\u003E = 147). The drug (500 mg\/d for 3 d) was administered on top of a standardized acute treatment of systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics, and subsequently continued for 3 months (250 mg\/2 d).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EC - Placebo (\u003Ci\u003En\u003C\/i\u003E = 154)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EO -\u0026nbsp; The TF rate within 3 months was 49% in the azithromycin group and 60% in the placebo group (\u0026nbsp;\u003Ci\u003EP\u003C\/i\u003E = 0.0526). Treatment intensification, step-up in hospital care, and mortality rates within 3 months were 47% versus 60% (\u003Ci\u003EP\u003C\/i\u003E = 0.0272), 13% versus 28% (\u003Ci\u003EP\u003C\/i\u003E = 0.0024), and 2% versus 4% (\u003Ci\u003EP\u003C\/i\u003E = 0.5075) in the azithromycin and placebo groups, respectively.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThree months of azithromycin for an infectious AECOPD requiring hospitalization may significantly reduce TF during the highest-risk period. Prolonged treatment seems to be necessary to maintain clinical benefits.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.atsjournals.org\/doi\/full\/10.1164\/rccm.201901-0094OC\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.atsjournals.org\/doi\/full\/10.1164\/rccm.201901-0094OC\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, the efficacy of nebulized budesonide, oral prednisolone, and placebo\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EP - 199 patients with acute exacerbations of COPD requiring hospitalization.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI - 2 mg of budesonide every 6 h (n = 71)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI-\u0026nbsp; 30 mg of oral prednisolone every 12 h (n = 62), C - Placebo (n = 66)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EO - The mean change (95% confidence interval) in postbronchodilator FEV(1) from H(0) to H(72) was greater with active treatments than with placebo: budesonide versus placebo, 0.10 L (0.02 to 0.18 L); prednisolone versus placebo, 0.16 L (0.08 to 0.24 L). The difference in FEV(1) between budesonide and prednisolone was not significant, -0.06 L (-0.14 to 0.02 L). The occurrence of serious adverse events was similar for all groups. Budesonide had less systemic activity than prednisolone as indicated by a higher incidence of hyperglycemia observed with prednisolone. Both budesonide and prednisolone improved airflow in COPD patients with acute exacerbations when compared with placebo.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/11874817\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/11874817\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3. What was the cause for the exacerbation?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ECOPD has been exacerbated secondary to right heart failure\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4. Could the ATT have affected her symptoms? If so how?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EYes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EFacial puffiness and pedal edema could be due to the renal or hepatic dysfunction caused secondary to the use of ATT medications.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ERifampicin among the ATT drugs is most commonly associated to cause AKI followed by isonizid and ethambutol\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EHepatic dysfunction is most common with Pyrazinamide followed by Isonizide, Rifampicin, Rthambutol.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E5.What could be the causes for her electrolyte imbalance?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHyponatremia in patients with\u0026nbsp;right heart failure is primarily caused by increased activity of arginine vasopressin (AVP). AVP increases free-water reabsorption in the renal collecting ducts, increasing blood volume and diluting plasma sodium concentrations.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2) Neurology (10 Marks)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA)\u0026nbsp;Link to patient details:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?q=https:\/\/143vibhahegde.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/wernickes-encephalopathy.html\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1621876726811000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNGuWt4y6-P9juTa-Kp497z1hGI8bQ\" href=\"https:\/\/143vibhahegde.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/wernickes-encephalopathy.html\" rel=\"noreferrer noreferrer noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/143vibhahegde.\u003Cwbr\u003Eblogspot.com\/2021\/05\/\u003Cwbr\u003Ewernickes-encephalopathy.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1) What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E40 year old man, diabetic since 2 years on irregular medications and regular alcoholic and smoker since 12 years with the history of 2-3 episodes of seizures 1 year back, presented with\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EIrrelevant talking , forgetfulness and reduced appetite since 9 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2) What are mechanism of action, indication and efficacy over placebo of each of the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used for this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EA Randomized, double-blind, multidose study of thiamin treatment\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E107 subjects who were detoxifying from alcohol. Five groups of subjects were assessed with the Mini-Mental State Examination and were examined for the presence of neurological signs. Subjects were given different doses of intramuscular thiamin for two consecutive days. The posttreatment performance of these groups then was examined on a test of working memory derived from comparative neuropsychology, namely, the delayed alternation task.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EOn the posttreatment measure, a superior performance was found in the group that received the highest dose of thiamin, compared with the other four treatment groups.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/11198705\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/11198705\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3) Why have neurological symptoms appeared this time, that were absent during withdrawal earlier? What could be a possible cause for this?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThe neurological symptoms are because the patient is in\u0026nbsp; Wernicke's encephalopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EAnd the probable other differentials are\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EUremic encephalopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EAlcohol withdrawal\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4) What is the reason for giving thiamine in this patient?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThiamine is present in the body as free thiamine, as well as in several phosphorylated forms: thiamine mono-phosphate (TMP), thiamine diphosphate (TDP), and thiamine triphosphate (TTP). TDP also called thiamine pyrophosphate, is the metabolically active and the most abundant form of thiamine in the body (\u0026gt;80%). Thiamine plays essential coenzyme and non-coenzyme roles in energy transformation, synthesis of pentoses and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate(NADPH), and membrane and nerve conduction. In energy transformation, thiamine is a cofactor in multiple enzyme complexes involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and amino acids, particularly pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH), and\u0026nbsp;\u003Cfont face=\"Symbol\" size=\"2\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003Ea\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (\u003Cfont face=\"Symbol\" size=\"2\"\u003E\u003Ci\u003Ea\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/font\u003E–KGDH).\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgUWK4jfJ1y2H7CSLIcRQ7GmN1DgOiVC6STekOy5RK6b1I_H4s7HfMAG0VBZ0HUFRQWObxiTVuIZdO7dby7i79kUrUX3zDEPMocpneeuldsz6uZqtFU8uT38wVNkTM2KAKRTpuROlIe6_w\/s1600\/1623399181425555-0.png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgUWK4jfJ1y2H7CSLIcRQ7GmN1DgOiVC6STekOy5RK6b1I_H4s7HfMAG0VBZ0HUFRQWObxiTVuIZdO7dby7i79kUrUX3zDEPMocpneeuldsz6uZqtFU8uT38wVNkTM2KAKRTpuROlIe6_w\/s1600\/1623399181425555-0.png\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Ca href=\"http:\/\/www.indianpediatrics.net\/aug2019\/aug-673-681.htm\"\u003Ehttp:\/\/www.indianpediatrics.net\/aug2019\/aug-673-681.htm\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThiamine is an important nutrient required to metabolize glucose used by the brain for energy. The lack of thiamine affects brain functions in the most metabolically active brain regions, including the activity of the hypothalamus which regulates temperature, appetite, emotions and growth. Thiamine deficiency affects the cells of the nervous and cardiovascular systems to a greater degree than the cells of other organ systems.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Alcohol reduces the absorption of thiamine by the body, diminishes stores of thiamine in the liver and hampers the activity of the enzyme that converts thiamine into an active state.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThiamine is given intravenously because abdominal absorption can be hampered in affected individuals. Mental status changes, vision abnormalities and ataxia all usually improve upon administration of thiamine. Thiamine administration may continue daily for\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/rarediseases.org\/rare-diseases\/wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/rarediseases.org\/rare-diseases\/wernicke-korsakoff-syndrome\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E5) What is the probable reason for kidney injury in this patient?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThe probable cause for her kidney injury could be due to alcoholism leading to dehydration, Pre renal AKI\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; What is the probable cause for the normocytic anemia?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn order to develop a diagnostic approach to the common problem of anemia associated with alcoholism, 121 chronic alcoholics admitted to a general medical service with a low hematocrit were evaluated.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMultiple contributing causes of anemia were present in most patients. Megaloblastic marrow change was found in 33.9% of patients, sideroblastic change in 23.1%, absent iron stores in 13.2%, aggregated macrophage iron in 81.0%, and acute blood loss in 24.8%.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3747828\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3747828\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EApart from reduced red blood cell production in the bone marrow there could be loss of blood from ulcer and artificial prosthesis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E7) Could chronic alcoholism have aggravated the foot ulcer formation? If yes, how and why?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient is already a known diabetic and has been on a poor diabetic control.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiabetes is known to cause peripheral neuropathy, more likelihood of developing wounds and ulcers with a slow healing process.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAlcohol on top of that also is known to cause thiamine deficiency which eventually leads leads peripheral neuropathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Alcohol can exert direct and indirect effects on nerve cell function. The direct effects of alcohol result from its metabolism to its toxic byproduct acetaldehyde. Acetaldehyde produced in the liver is transported to the periphery where it can form protein adducts and cause nerve damage. The conversion of alcohol to acetaldehyde also results in the formation of reactive oxygen species, which can exert deleterious effects on peripheral nerve physiology and function. Alcohol enhances protein kinase C e (PKCe) levels and activity in dorsal root ganglia. Administration of PKCe inhibitors reduces ethanol-induced mechanical hyperalgesia. Chronic ethanol exposure can impair both anterograde and retrograde axonal transport. PKCe could also regulate alcohols effects on axonal transport through its interactions with the cytoskeleton. Ethanol impairs Schwann cell proliferation and myelin sheath formation. Alcohol can also mediate indirect effects on nerve cell function by reducing absorption, hepatic storage, and phosphorylation of thiamine. class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDuration of treatment and follow-up was 18 months. The primary endpoint was a composite of ischaemic stroke, myocardial infarction, vascular death, or rehospitalisation for acute ischaemia\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E596 (15.7%) patients reached the primary endpoint in the group receiving aspirin and clopidogrel compared with 636 (16·7%) in the clopidogrel alone group. Life-threatening bleedings were higher in the group receiving aspirin and clopidogrel versus clopidogrel alone.Major bleedings were also increased in the group receiving aspirin and clopidogrel but no difference was recorded in mortality.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAdding aspirin to clopidogrel in high-risk patients with recent ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack is associated with a non-significant difference in reducing major vascular events. However, the risk of life-threatening or major bleeding is increased by the addition of aspirin\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETRIAL ON ASPIRIN VS PLACEBO\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" readability=\"7\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/onlinelibrary.wiley.com\/doi\/full\/10.1111\/j.1365-2796.2003.01233.x\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPatients with ischaemic stroke but not complete paresis were included. Totally, 441 patients (220 aspirin, 221 placebo) completed the trial.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe trial was randomized, double-blind and placebo-controlled.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETablets Aspirin 325 mg or placebo, water solvable, were administered orally once a day for five consecutive days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENeurological assessments were carried out three times daily during the treatment period to detect progression of at least two points in the Scandinavian Stroke Supervision Scale.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient outcome was followed up at discharge and at 3 months.Aspirin treatment did not significantly reduce the frequency of stroke progression. Amongst aspirin‐treated patients, stroke progression occurred in 15.9% as compared with 16.7% in the placebo group, which is less frequent than expected. The relative risk was 0.95 (95% CI 0.62–1.45) in the treatment group.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAs regards patient outcome at discharge and after 3 months, aspirin treatment did not show any difference.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E4) Does the patients history of alcoholism make him more susceptible to ischaemic or haemorrhagic type of stroke?\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EModerate\u0026nbsp;and high\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 13.3333px;\"\u003E \u003C\/span\u003Eintakes of alcohol have been documented to have acute potentially deleterious physiologic effects within hours after consumption, including impaired fibrinolysis\u0026nbsp;and increased platelet activation, blood pressure and heart rate.\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EThe Stroke Onset Study was conducted in three medical centers. This study\u0026nbsp; utilized a case-crossover study design to assess the change in risk of acute ischemic stroke onset during a brief “hazard period” following consumption of alcohol.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E390 patients were interviewed between January 2001 and November 2006\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EThe alcohol consumption was associated with a transient increased risk of ischemic stroke in the subsequent hour that was 2.3 times higher than the risk during periods with no alcohol consumption. The risk returned to baseline by three hours and there was a modestly lower risk by 24 hours.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC2937356\/#!po=33.7838\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC2937356\/#!po=33.7838\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EEthanol intoxication as a risk factor for ischaemic stroke was studied\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E100 patients (67 men, 33 women) aged from 15-55 with acute ischemic brain infarction were studied.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EIn 40 cases the onset of symptoms was preceded within 24 hours by ethanol intoxication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Ethanol intoxication preceding brain infarction was 4-7 times as common in men and 6-15 times as common in women as ethanol intoxication. Nineteen of the patients were heavy drinkers. Heavy drinking was twice as common in men and 5 times as common in women as heavy drinking.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv Is there any relationship between occurrence of seizure to brain stroke. If yes what is the mechanism behind it?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThere are several causes for early onset seizures after ischaemic strokes. An increase in intracellular Ca\u003Csup\u003E2\u003C\/sup\u003E\u003Csup\u003E+\u003C\/sup\u003E\u0026nbsp;and Na\u003Csup\u003E+\u003C\/sup\u003E\u0026nbsp;with a resultant lower threshold for depolarisation, glutamate excitotoxicity, hypoxia, metabolic dysfunction, global hypoperfusion, and hyperperfusion injury have all been postulated as putative neurofunctional aetiologies. Seizures after haemorrhagic strokes are thought to be attributable to irritation caused by products of blood metabolism.\u0026nbsp; Late onset seizures are associated with the persistent changes in neuronal excitability and gliotic scarring is most probably the underlying cause.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC2585721\/#:~:text=The%2520exact%2520pathophysiology%2520is%2520unclear,most%2520probably%2520the%2520underlying%2520cause.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC2585721\/#:~:text=The%20exact%20pathophysiology%20is%20unclear,most%20probably%20the%20underlying%20cause.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2. In the previous episodes of seizures, patient didn't loose his consciousness but in the recent episode he lost his consciousness what might be the reason?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThe patient had a GTCS this time dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E2) What was the reason for his IC bleed? Does Alcoholism contribute to bleeding diatheses ?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EYes, alcohol are noted to cause strokes especially hemorrhagic infarcts.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EModerate\u0026nbsp;and high\u0026nbsp;intakes of alcohol have been documented to have acute potentially deleterious physiologic effects within hours after consumption, including impaired fibrinolysis\u0026nbsp;and increased platelet activation, blood pressure and heart rate.\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EThe Stroke Onset Study was conducted in three medical centers. This study\u0026nbsp; utilized a case-crossover study design to assess the change in risk of acute ischemic stroke onset during a brief “hazard period” following consumption of alcohol.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E390 patients were interviewed between January 2001 and November 2006\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003EThe alcohol consumption was associated with a transient increased risk of ischemic stroke in the subsequent hour that was 2.3 times higher than the risk during periods with no alcohol consumption. The risk returned to baseline by three hours and there was a modestly lower risk by 24 hours.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv A meta analysis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"article__body\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"container\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"row\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"col-md-7 col-lg-9 article__sections\"\u003E\u003Csection\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E18 254 patients were assessed, and of these 13 946 (76%) had sinus rhythm and 3066 (17%) had atrial fibrillation at baseline. Crude death rates over a mean follow-up of 1·5 years were 16% (2237 of 13 945) in patients with sinus rhythm and 21% (633 of 3064) in patients with atrial fibrillation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003Eβ-blocker therapy led to a significant reduction in all-cause mortality in patients with sinus rhythm (p\u0026lt;0·001), but not in patients with atrial fibrillation (p=0·73), with a significant p value for interaction of baseline rhythm (p=0·002).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;β blockers didn't improve prognosis in patients with concomitant heart failure and atrial fibrillation.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.thelancet.com\/journals\/lancet\/article\/PIIS0140-6736(14)61373-8\/fulltext\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.thelancet.com\/journals\/lancet\/article\/PIIS0140-6736(14)61373-8\/fulltext\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"section-paragraph\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E3) What is the pathogenesis of renal involvement due to heart failure (cardio renal syndrome)? It's mandatory to keep reviewing the Aptt, PT, INR levels to adjust the dose and to look for any bleeding manifestations.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ED) Link to patient details:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?q=https:\/\/daddalavineeshachowdary.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/67-year-old-patient-with-acute-coronary.html?m%3D1\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1621876726811000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNGZBtZQGp7TQpdemfJlzdSBOxU7jQ\" href=\"https:\/\/daddalavineeshachowdary.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/67-year-old-patient-with-acute-coronary.html?m=1\" rel=\"noreferrer noreferrer noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/\u003Cwbr\u003Edaddalavineeshachowdary.\u003Cwbr\u003Eblogspot.com\/2021\/05\/67-year-\u003Cwbr\u003Eold-patient-with-acute-\u003Cwbr\u003Ecoronary.html?m=1\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EQuestions-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E1) What is the evolution of the symptomatology in this patient in terms of an event timeline and where is the anatomical localization for the problem and what is the primary etiology of the patient's problem?\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EKnown case of HTN and type 2 DM since 8 yrs\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EChest pain since 3 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EGiddiness \u0026amp; profuse sweating since 1 day\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EAnatomical localization -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EHeart : Inferior wall MI\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EPrimary Etiology -\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EAcute inferior wall MI\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EKnown case of Type 2 DM, HTN\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E2) What are mechanism of action, indication and efficacy over placebo of each of the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used for this patient?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EA double-blinded RCT comparing clopidogrel\u0026nbsp; to placebo in addition to aspirin in acute ST elevations MI\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EP - 12,562 patients who had presented within 24 hours after the onset of symptoms\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EI - clopidogrel (300 mg immediately, followed by 75 mg once daily) (6259 patients) in addition to aspirin for 3 to 12 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EC - Placebo ( 6303 patients) in addition to aspirin for 3 to 12 months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EO - The first primary outcome — a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or stroke — occurred in 9.3 percent of the patients in the clopidogrel group and 11.4 percent of the patients in the placebo group. The second primary outcome — the first primary outcome or refractory ischemia — occurred in 16.5 percent of the patients in the clopidogrel group and 18.8 percent of the patients in the placebo group.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThe percentages of patients with in-hospital refractory or severe ischemia, heart failure, and revascularization procedures were also significantly lower with clopidogrel. There were significantly more patients with major bleeding in the clopidogrel group than in the placebo group (3.7 percent vs. 2.7 percent; relative risk, 1.38; P=0.001), but there were not significantly more patients with episodes of life-threatening bleeding (2.1 percent vs. 1.8 percent, P=0.13) or hemorrhagic strokes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EThe antiplatelet agent clopidogrel has beneficial effects in patients with acute coronary syndromes without ST-segment elevation. However, the risk of major bleeding is increased among patients treated with clopidogrel.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv How is it related to pancreatitis?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe cause for his dyspnea is pleural effusion, secondary to pancreatitis.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETwo main causes of pleural effusion are transdiaphragmatic lymphatic blockage or pancreaticopleural fistulae secondary to leak and disruption of the pancreatic duct or pseudocyst caused by an episode of acute pancreatitis. The leak or disruption is more likely to lead to a pleural effusion if the duct disruption is posteriorly into the retroperitoneum. The pancreatic enzymes can track up into the mediastinum and then rupture into the pleural cavity either left side or bilaterally and so create a connection between the pancreatic duct and the pleural cavity.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4087768\/#:~:text=Two%2520main%2520causes%2520of%2520pleural,an%2520episode%2520of%2520acute%2520pancreatitis.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4087768\/#:~:text=Two%20main%20causes%20of%20pleural,an%20episode%20of%20acute%20pancreatitis.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) Name possible reasons why the patient has developed a state of hyperglycemia.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Why doesn't the child have the excessive urge of urination at night time ?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" readability=\"17.143401015228427\"\u003E\u003Cspan readability=\"12.631979695431472\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EChild has\u0026nbsp; urge to urinate during day time but during at night he is asleep without an urge to pass urine.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003EPsychosomatic overactive bladder\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E3. How would you want to manage the patient to relieve him of his symptoms?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" readability=\"17\"\u003E\u003Cspan readability=\"10\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003E'Treatment has traditionally been that of benign neglect with just an explanation of the condition, perhaps with some directed counseling regarding the putative stressor trigger.\u003Csup\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/sup\u003EThis involves reassuring the parents and child and waiting for the condition to self-resolve. Reducing dietary intake of oxalate-rich beverages such as tea and acidic juices such as apple in children who consume large amounts of them, along with liberal intake of water, have been proposed as ancillary approaches while riding the condition out.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA wait-and-see method does work, but it can take quite some time, requiring 1 to 5 months on average for the condition to go away, during which time the pollakiuria can continue to be disruptive to normal routines.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMedication is often tried; this would typically be an anticholinergic drug such as oxybutynin on the assumption that there is a form of bladder dyssynergy taking place. This has usually been reported to be ineffective, which is not surprising given that the problem in pollakiuria is felt to be sensory rather than motoric, and of course it is not without adverse effects such as drowsiness or dry mouth.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIndomethacin has also been proposed as a treatment, but there are no controlled studies looking at its value, and it is again with potential adverse effects.\u0026nbsp;Given this, and the fact that pollakiuria is a benign self-limited condition, there is no role for the use of medication as treatment. Similarly, biofeedback has been advanced as a therapeutic option in an uncontrolled study, with a long response time for effectiveness.\u0026nbsp;Although safe, this is again unproven and can be expensive.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.contemporarypediatrics.com\/view\/strategy-treat-pollakiuria\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.contemporarypediatrics.com\/view\/strategy-treat-pollakiuria\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv Can we prevent it?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;ART should be stopped and ATT needs to be initiated followed by ART initiation 6 weeks later.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E7) Infectious disease and Hepatology:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003ELink to patient details:\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Ca data-saferedirecturl=\"https:\/\/www.google.com\/url?q=https:\/\/kavyasamudrala.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/liver-abscess.html\u0026amp;source=gmail\u0026amp;ust=1621876726811000\u0026amp;usg=AFQjCNGE3wrZejQ9XODfHLfxdrlv1aIB4g\" href=\"https:\/\/kavyasamudrala.blogspot.com\/2021\/05\/liver-abscess.html\" rel=\"noreferrer noreferrer noreferrer\" target=\"_blank\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/kavyasamudrala.\u003Cwbr\u003Eblogspot.com\/2021\/05\/liver-\u003Cwbr\u003Eabscess.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E1. Do you think drinking locally made alcohol caused liver abscess in this patient due to predisposing factors\u0026nbsp;present in it ?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAmoebic liver abscess (ALA) seen commonly in the tropics is predominantly confined to adult males, especially those who consume locally brewed alcohol, although intestinal amoebiasis occurs in all age groups and in both genders.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC6077556\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC6077556\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. What is the etio-pathogenesis \u0026nbsp;of liver abscess in a chronic alcoholic patient ? ( since 30 years - 1 bottle per day)\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA retrospective study was conducted on 108 patients to find the role of alcoholism in liver abscess.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E'This study was undertaken on patients both male and female admitted in surgical wards of Chennai medical college \u0026amp; hospital. 108 patients were taken up for the study from the surgical wards of the hospital over a period of 1½ year i.e., from January 2013 to June 2014.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFollowing alcoholism, poor economic status \u0026amp; malnutrition also plays a vital role as predisposing factors in the formation of liver abscess. Among alcoholism also, consuming locally prepared alcohol plays a vital role, but the reason is still been unknown.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt was undoubtedly proved that alcoholism, mainly consuming locally prepared alcohol plays a major role as a predisposing factor for the formation of liver abscesses that is both amoebic as well as pyogenic liver abscess because of the adverse effects of alcohol over the Liver. It is also proven that Alcoholism is never an etiological factor for the formation of liver abscess'\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.msjonline.org\/index.php\/ijrms\/article\/view\/2414#:~:text=Conclusion%253AFrom%2520our%2520study%2520it,of%2520alcohol%2520over%2520the%2520Liver.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.msjonline.org\/index.php\/ijrms\/article\/view\/2414#:~:text=Conclusion%3AFrom%20our%20study%20it,of%20alcohol%20over%20the%20Liver\u003C\/a\u003E.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. Is liver abscess more common in right lobe ?\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E50% of solitary liver abscesses occur in the right lobe of the liver (a more significant part with more blood supply), less commonly in the left liver lobe or caudate lobe.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe right hepatic lobe receives blood from both the superior mesenteric and portal veins, whereas the left hepatic lobe receives inferior mesenteric and splenic drainage. It also contains a denser network of biliary canaliculi and, overall, accounts for more hepatic mass. Studies have suggested that a streaming effect in the portal circulation is causative.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK538230\/#:~:text=The%2520usual%2520pattern%2520of%2520abscess,by%2520location%2520in%2520the%2520liver.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK538230\/#:~:text=The%20usual%20pattern%20of%20abscess,by%20location%20in%20the%20liver\u003C\/a\u003E.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4.What are the indications for ultrasound guided aspiration of liver abscess ?\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ecomplicated diverticular abscess\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ECrohn's disease related abscess\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Ecomplicated appendicitis with appendicular abscess\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Etuboovarian abscess\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003Epost-surgical fluid
